parameters.content:
## Trellis: Scheduled Post Publisher

**This workflow is what makes scheduling real.** Before it existed, Social Hub only ever
marked a post "scheduled" in the browser's localStorage — nothing on the server ever
looked at that row again, so the post never actually went out. This workflow is the missing
half: it polls the `scheduled_social_posts` table on the Hub every **10 minutes**, finds rows
that are due, and hands each one off to the existing Instagram/Facebook publish webhooks
(`B3-social-publisher-v2.json` and the Facebook equivalent).

### Cadence
Schedule Trigger fires every 10 minutes → 144 runs/day. Most runs find nothing due and must
no-op quietly (see "No Due Posts?" below) — this is normal, not an error.

### FLOW
Schedule Trigger → **Fetch Due Posts** (GET `scheduled_social_posts` where
`status=eq.scheduled` AND `scheduled_for=lte.<now>`, ordered oldest-first, capped at 20/run so
a big backlog can never stampede the publish webhooks) → **Normalize Due Posts** (Code:
flattens the response into one item per row regardless of how the HTTP node shaped the array)
→ **No Due Posts?** (IF: with zero rows nothing downstream executes — n8n simply has no
items to run the rest of the graph on, so the execution ends cleanly with no writes and no
error) → **Claim Post** → **Drop Unclaimed Posts** → **Route by Platform** →
**Publish Instagram** / **Publish Facebook** → **Publish Succeeded?** →
**Mark Published** or **Prepare Failure** → **Mark Failed**.

### THE DOUBLE-PUBLISH GUARD (read this before touching Claim Post)
Double-posting to a customer's Instagram or Facebook is the worst failure mode this workflow
can produce, and with a 10-minute poll it is very possible for two executions to overlap (a
slow prior run, a manual "execute now", n8n queue catch-up after downtime, etc.).

**Claim Post** PATCHes the row with a *conditional* filter:
`?id=eq.{id}&status=eq.scheduled` and header `Prefer: return=representation`. PostgREST only
updates (and only returns) a row when BOTH the id AND status match at the moment the PATCH
runs. That means:
- If this run is the first to reach the row, the PATCH matches, flips it to `publishing`,
  bumps `attempts`, and returns the updated row (array with 1 element).
- If another run already claimed it first (its status is no longer `scheduled`), the WHERE
  clause matches nothing, and PostgREST returns an **empty array** — even though the HTTP
  call itself succeeds with 200/204.

**Drop Unclaimed Posts** (Code node right after Claim Post) is the enforcement point: it reads
each Claim Post response and keeps only rows that actually came back non-empty. Any item whose
claim returned no row is silently dropped — it does NOT get published again, because some
other execution already has it. This is the only thing standing between this workflow and a
customer getting the same post published twice, so don't remove or "simplify" it.

If the Claim Post HTTP call itself errors (network/5xx, not just an empty match), the item is
routed to **Claim Error - Leave Scheduled** and dropped WITHOUT touching the row — it stays
`status=scheduled` and will simply be picked up again on the next 10-minute run. That is
intentional: we only know for certain a claim failed, not whether it *actually* changed
anything on the row, so the safe default is "leave it alone, try again later", not
"guess and mark it failed".

### PUBLISH STEP — CHECK THE BODY, NOT JUST THE HTTP STATUS
`trellis-social-publish` / `trellis-facebook-publish` are the existing synchronous publish
webhooks (see `services/socialService.ts` → `publishToSocial()` / `publishToFacebook()` for
the contract this mirrors). They can return **HTTP 200 with `{ success: false, error: ... }`**
when the platform API rejects the post — an HTTP-level 200 is NOT proof of a successful
publish. **Publish Succeeded?** explicitly checks `success === true` in the response body
before routing to **Mark Published**; anything else (including a same-shaped `success:false`
body or a genuine HTTP/network error from either publish node) goes to **Prepare Failure** →
**Mark Failed**.

### NO SILENT RETRIES
**Mark Failed** sets `status='failed'` and `last_error` (truncated to ~500 chars) and stops
there — a failed post does NOT automatically retry. `attempts` is tracked on every claim
specifically so a future bounded-retry policy (e.g. "re-queue if attempts < 3") can be added
later; today it's informational only. A human reviews `failed` rows in the UI and decides
whether to re-schedule.

### PREREQUISITE SQL
Already applied on the live Hub (`horvjqqifgrzxesuxtfm`); mirrored in `constants.ts`
`SQL_SCHEMA` for the record (search for "SCHEDULED SOCIAL POSTS"):
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scheduled_social_posts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),
  branch_id UUID NOT NULL,
  branch_slug TEXT,
  platform TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'instagram' CHECK (platform IN ('instagram', 'facebook')),
  caption TEXT NOT NULL,
  media_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'image' CHECK (media_type IN ('image', 'video', 'carousel')),
  media_urls JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  scheduled_for TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled'
    CHECK (status IN ('scheduled', 'publishing', 'published', 'failed', 'cancelled')),
  attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error TEXT,
  post_id TEXT,
  published_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  source TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'upload',
  created_by UUID,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);
-- + idx_ssp_due (partial, WHERE status='scheduled'), idx_ssp_branch_scheduled,
-- RLS enabled (service_role ALL + anon/authenticated ALL), grants, updated_at trigger.
```

### SETUP REQUIRED
1. Import this workflow into n8n.
2. Every Supabase HTTP Request node (**Fetch Due Posts**, **Claim Post**, **Mark Published**,
   **Mark Failed**) uses *Predefined Credential Type* (`supabaseApi`) pointed at the same
   **Sproutify Trellis** credential already used by `B2-campaign-dispatch.json`
   (`Save Send Ids` / `Mark Complete`) — no service-role key is pasted into this workflow.
   If that credential isn't in your instance yet, create a Supabase API credential named
   "Sproutify Trellis" pointed at the Hub project with the service_role key, and re-select it
   on each of those four nodes.
3. **Publish Instagram** / **Publish Facebook** call the existing public webhooks directly
   (`https://n8n.sproutify.app/webhook/trellis-social-publish` and
   `.../trellis-facebook-publish`) — no credential needed, same as the frontend's own fetch
   calls in `socialService.ts`.
4. Run once manually against a test row, then activate the workflow.

### NOTES
- `branch_id` sent to the publish webhooks is always the branch **UUID** stored on the row
  (never the domain slug) — matches the contract in `socialService.ts`.
- `image_url` sent to the publish webhooks is always `media_urls[0]` (or null for a
  Facebook text-only post with no media).
- `scheduled_for` sent to the publish webhooks is always `null` — by the time this workflow
  calls them, the post is being published *now*; scheduling already happened at the
  `scheduled_social_posts` layer.

nodes.name: Fetch Due Posts
nodes.notes: GET scheduled_social_posts where status=eq.scheduled AND scheduled_for=lte.now, oldest first, capped at 20/run so one backlog can't stampede the publish webhooks. Runs every 10 minutes (144x/day) -- most runs find nothing due.

nodes.name: No Due Posts?
nodes.notes: With zero rows due, n8n has no items to run this (or anything downstream) on -- the execution simply ends here with no writes and no error. That's the intended no-op for the 143+ runs/day that find nothing to publish.

nodes.name: Claim Post
nodes.notes: DOUBLE-PUBLISH GUARD: PATCH is filtered on id=eq.{id} AND status=eq.scheduled, so it only matches (and only updates attempts/status) if this run got here first. Prefer: return=representation means a row already claimed by another overlapping run comes back as an EMPTY array here -- see 'Drop Unclaimed Posts' next, which is what actually enforces the guard. A genuine HTTP/network error on this call (not an empty match) routes to 'Claim Error - Leave Scheduled' -- the row stays status=scheduled and is retried on the next 10-minute run rather than being guessed at.

nodes.name: Claim Error - Leave Scheduled
nodes.notes: Claim Post itself errored (network/5xx), not a normal 'already claimed' empty match. We don't know whether the PATCH actually landed, so the safe default is to touch nothing and let the row (still status=scheduled) get picked up again on the next run, instead of guessing and marking it failed.

nodes.name: Drop Unclaimed Posts
nodes.notes: Enforces the double-publish guard: keeps only items whose Claim Post response actually returned a row (this run won the claim). Items whose claim came back empty (another run already claimed that row) are dropped here -- never published, never touched again by this run.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ branch_id: $json.branch_id, caption: $json.caption, image_url: (Array.isArray($json.media_urls) && $json.media_urls.length ? $json.media_urls[0] : null), media_type: $json.media_type || 'image', media_urls: $json.media_urls || [], scheduled_for: null }) }}

nodes.name: Publish Instagram
nodes.notes: Matches the trellis-social-publish contract used by publishToSocial() in services/socialService.ts. branch_id is the branch UUID stored on the row; image_url is always media_urls[0]; scheduled_for is null because this IS the send, right now. RESPONSE HANDLING: raw TEXT body with neverError+fullResponse, so an unreadable reply can't masquerade as a publish failure. 'Interpret Publish Result' decides the outcome, not the HTTP node.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ branch_id: $json.branch_id, caption: $json.caption, image_url: (Array.isArray($json.media_urls) && $json.media_urls.length ? $json.media_urls[0] : null), scheduled_for: null }) }}

nodes.name: Publish Facebook
nodes.notes: Matches the trellis-facebook-publish contract used by publishToFacebook() in services/socialService.ts. image_url is optional -- Facebook allows text-only posts, so a post with no media sends image_url: null. RESPONSE HANDLING: raw TEXT body with neverError+fullResponse, so an unreadable reply can't masquerade as a publish failure. 'Interpret Publish Result' decides the outcome, not the HTTP node.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ status: 'published', published_at: new Date().toISOString(), post_id: $json.post_id || null }) }}

nodes.name: Prepare Failure
nodes.notes: Normalizes both failure shapes (HTTP error output vs. { success: false, error }) into { id, last_error } for Mark Failed. Always resolves id via 'Drop Unclaimed Posts' since the failure body itself may not carry it.

nodes.name: Mark Failed
nodes.notes: Terminal state. Does NOT auto-retry -- attempts is tracked on every claim specifically so a future bounded-retry policy can be layered on top, but today a failed row just sits there for a human to review and, if appropriate, re-schedule.

nodes.name: Interpret Publish Result
nodes.notes: Decides published / failed / needs_review. needs_review exists because an unreadable reply after a 2xx most likely means the post DID go out - recording that as 'failed' would invite a retry and double-post.

nodes.name: Mark Needs Review
nodes.notes: Terminal, and deliberately NOT 'failed'. The post probably went out; a human checks the account and decides. Never auto-retried.
